question: A 41-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by ambulance because of a sudden onset severe headache. On presentation, the patient also says that she is not able to see well. Physical examination shows ptosis of the right eye with a dilated pupil that is deviated inferiorly and laterally. Based on the clinical presentation, neurosurgery is immediately consulted and the patient is taken for an early trans-sphenoidal surgical decompression. Which of the following will also most likely need to be supplemented in this patient?
analysis: The clinical presentation of a sudden onset severe headache with ptosis of the right eye, dilated pupil, and visual disturbances is concerning for an acute pituitary apoplexy, which is a medical emergency requiring urgent surgical decompression. In this scenario, corticosteroids are most likely to be supplemented to manage the acute adrenal insufficiency that can occur due to pituitary gland dysfunction.
